limitations: One task adapter, one Auth process registration, two durable jobs and two sequential Auth owners. Covers timer ownership, already admitted claims, abort before invocation or a further claim, network settlement, receipt and shutdown. Empty ticks and task-adapter queries are abstracted.

Conformance runs the production embedded Auth listener, scheduler, signed HTTPS dispatcher and file-backed PGlite queue with a local receiver. It verifies delivery after adapter detach, a Core task after Auth shutdown, durable 200 and 503 receipts, and the next claim after restart. Hosted PostgreSQL and Redis shutdown remain outside the runtime check.

The proof assumes claim and receipt storage operations settle. The companion immediate fan-out projection covers admitted request deliveries. Lease expiry and reclamation, future retry timing, startup rollback and shutdown errors remain outside this projection. No wall-clock completion guarantee is proved.

One admitted SIWE request, one tenant, two local destinations, one unreadable stored secret, and one healthy immediate delivery. Request response, sibling settlement and runtime shutdown can interleave.
Real conformance verifies the signature, distinguishes the immediate request owner from the periodic worker, and reopens file-backed PGlite to read the committed receipt.

Requests that emit after listener retirement, transaction-bound deferred delivery, larger fan-outs, native storage failure and hosted PostgreSQL/Redis closure remain outside this projection. Progress assumes the original HTTP and storage operations settle.
